tasks.short: Collect leave, availability and machine status, plan the work schedule in a spreadsheet, decide the crew and machine assignments, and tell workers their shifts.

steps.what: Workers enter leave and availability in the scheduling app
Farm supervisor collects leave requests, availability and machine status: by phone and messages today; after the change reads them in the app and chases the gaps
Farm supervisor plans work schedules in a spreadsheet according to personnel and equipment availability
Farm supervisor decides crew and machine assignments and resolves clashes
Farm supervisor checks the final schedule: every job has a crew and machine, skills fit, leave and rest times are respected
Farm supervisor publishes the checked schedule to the workers' app
Farm supervisor tells workers their shifts: posts the paper schedule and phones changes today; phones only same-day changes and workers without the app after the change

tasks.design: Workers enter leave and availability in a scheduling app on their phone, and machines out of use come from the maintenance list ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the supervisor does not collect them by phone. Fixed rules fill a first schedule from the week's work, the available workers' skills and the free machines, and mark clashes. The supervisor decides assignments, resolves clashes, checks the schedule and publishes it to each worker's app, so only same-day changes are phoned.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability came by phone and the schedule was built by hand in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling apps take availability from workers and fill schedules by rules.
tasks.still_hard: Seasonal workers change availability at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Pairing a new worker with someone who will teach them.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor decides assignments instead of building the grid.

evidence.claim: Scheduling apps can take availability from workers and fill shifts by rules.
Order-driven planning touches no AI Act Annex III area; no performance scoring is used.
A system holding staff data needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from next week due to workers told; hiring seasonal staff is outside.
Input contract: workers use the app; fallback is phone and paper.
Workers enter availability (s0, share 1) in about the time a phone call took; this is outside the supervisor's savings.

Assignment decisions, the schedule check and publishing stay with the supervisor at full time. s1 keeps 30 for reading entries and chasing gaps. s2 keeps 50 because the supervisor still adjusts the first schedule. s4 keeps 40 for same-day changes and workers without the app.

incremental.description: Farm supervisor keeps skills and scheduling rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The week's schedule with crews, machines and shifts exactly as checked by the supervisor in s3c, published once to the workers in the scheduling app; any change needs a new check and publication.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small permanent crew where many workers do not use the app, so availability and shifts still go by phone (29.8); high: a large seasonal crew using the app (41.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farm supervisor keeps deciding assignments and resolving clashes; collecting availability, building the grid and phoning shifts shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time with the crew.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
